_comment: Pinned Piper voice per actor type, French arm (spec 11.2, 14.1.1). Same append-only rule as voices.json: NEVER change one of these after French scenarios exist -- a voice is the only cue distinguishing one actor from another, so swapping one silently invalidates every provenance question in the bank. Adding a voice requires regenerating the French bank.
quality_note: Piper's French catalogue does not clear the bar voices.json set for English: only 4 single-identity voices exist at medium quality or above (siwis, tom, and upmc's two named speakers), against 6 actor types, and no 'high' French model exists at all. Rather than share a voice between two actor types -- which would break the 'a voice is never shared' rule in spec 11.4 and make provenance questions unanswerable -- this file spends two 'low' quality models (gilles, mls_1840) to reach six, placed on the two roles where the compromise costs the least: cargo (low-priority traffic, per its own English rationale) and system (already run through the pa_intercom filter, which band-limits and compresses hard enough that a stronger source model would not survive it intact anyway). Revisit this file, not the rule, when Piper ships more French voices.

security.why: Male, medium quality, single speaker. Security speaks in every phase and during the finale, so -- as in the English set -- it gets a clean, unshared voice rather than one of the two quality compromises.

construction.why: Pierre, the male half of the two-speaker `upmc` model, medium quality. A named, fixed speaker id inside a 2-speaker corpus is not the 'unstable to pin' problem the English set rejected `libritts`/`arctic`/`vctk` for -- that objection was about selecting one voice out of 18-904 anonymous ones. Two named speakers pin exactly like two separate single-speaker models.

cargo.why: Male, low quality -- the first of the two quality compromises (see quality_note). Spent here because English's own cargo entry calls it the 'third male voice... low-priority traffic': the least salient human role is where weaker audio costs the least.

medical.why: Female, medium quality, single speaker, from the well-established SIWIS corpus. The best available female voice, on the role English also gave its best voice to ('calm and precise, which suits Medical').

civilian.why: Jessica, the female half of the `upmc` pair, medium quality. Distinct model and corpus from siwis, which is what keeps it apart from Medical -- the same 'separate the two female British voices by accent' logic the English set used for Civilian, applied here as a separate recording rather than a separate accent.

system.why: The second quality compromise (see quality_note), and deliberately the one spent here rather than on a human actor: the `pa_intercom` filter below band-limits and hard-compresses every system line regardless of source quality, so this is the one role where a low-quality model and a medium-quality one would end up sounding closer together than anywhere else in the set. Speaker 1840 of the MLS French corpus is anonymised in its own metadata -- gender unconfirmed, and irrelevant here the way it is not for a human actor, since the filter is what tells the player 'this is the station, not a person', not the voice underneath it.

pa_intercom.purpose: Same filter and same purpose as the English set: make automated station announcements instantly recognisable as machine-spoken, so a provenance question never mistakes the station for a seventh person.
pa_intercom.note: Band-limits to telephone/intercom range and compresses hard. Applied at generation time only; the runtime plays the rendered file as-is.

distinctness_matrix._comment: The weakest pair is what determines whether provenance is answerable. Reviewed pairwise at pinning time, same as voices.json.
distinctness_matrix.sexes: 3 male (security, construction, cargo), 2 female (medical, civilian), 1 unconfirmed (system, moot behind the intercom filter)
distinctness_matrix.models: tom, upmc/pierre, gilles (male); siwis, upmc/jessica (female); mls_1840 (system)
distinctness_matrix.weakest_pair: construction (upmc/pierre) vs civilian (upmc/jessica) -- same underlying corpus, separated only by the model's own two trained speakers rather than by a different dataset the way every English pair is. The next weakest is cargo (gilles-low) against the medium-quality voices generally: audibly lower fidelity, which is the cost quality_note describes rather than a distinctness problem.
distinctness_matrix.system_separation: system is additionally separated from all five human voices by the pa_intercom filter, exactly as in the English set

rejected.fr_FR-mls-medium: 125-speaker multi-speaker model with anonymous numeric ids; speaker selection inside it is not stable enough to pin -- the same reasoning that rejected en_US-libritts-high, en_US-arctic-medium and en_GB-vctk-medium
rejected.fr_FR-siwis-low: superseded by fr_FR-siwis-medium, same speaker at higher quality
